parts.text: The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured old man with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin with age spots, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a large ear with a fat hanging lobe, thick neck, hunched broad shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Head type: a huge tall lumpy dome skull with dents and bumps, like the master reference, pink flesh-toned clay skin, a dirty, worn plain beige trucker cap with a mesh back, completely blank with no logo, signatures or writing, messy grey hair sticking out at the sides. No mask: a weathered wrinkled face with huge round bulging staring eyes in baggy lids, a big nose and a scraggly grey-brown beard and moustache. Wearing a battered, scuffed black leather jacket with a zip front, open over a plain faded grey T-shirt with no lettering or print, in his left hand he holds out a round cracked bone-white clay orb shaped like a goalie mask rolled into a ball, covered in rows of small breathing holes with rusty rivets and dried blood; it is all one off-white colour, with no red half, no band and no button; his right fist grips a rusty hatchet with a worn wooden handle, held low at his side. A plain textured terracotta-orange pressed clay backdrop. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands are full: the orb held out in one hand toward the viewer, the hatchet gripped in the other. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora, red and white ball, ball with a centre button, writing on clothes, logo on cap

A grotesque disfigured clay WOMAN (female, not the man in the reference: copy only the reference's clay style, pose and framing) with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a thin neck and narrow hunched shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Deep dark-brown clay skin, a battered dented black top hat with a torn brim and a faded checkered band, tufts of greasy grey hair under it, raised blue clay veins on the forehead. No mask: her disfigured face is bare, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red lids, a crooked broken nose and rotten yellow teeth. Wearing a long battered dark plum greatcoat with a ragged high collar, honey stains down the front and a few clay bees crawling on the shoulder, a worn leather bandolier strap slung diagonally across her chest from shoulder to hip with exactly five small wrinkled shrunken heads hanging from it, their eyes and lips stitched shut, wisps of dark hair, her right fist grips a rusty hunting knife with a pitted, chipped blade smeared with blood, a heavy sledgehammer slung on her back. A rusty orange pressed-clay backdrop. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, her body is in three-quarter view and her head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Her right hand grips the held weapon in a tight clenched fist seen from the back of the hand, knuckles toward the camera, palm hidden, the blade angled up and out; her other hand hangs open.
